title: Deterministic billing attribution for batched embeddings, rerank selections and tool-generated tokens
creator: Asha Patel
description: Summary: Production reports and customer tickets show inconsistent token/embedding charges for non-chat endpoints when requests include batching, reranker scoring, or tool-call derived downstream model invocations (structured outputs: 'tool_result' fields). Root cause analysis found three contributing issues: 1) Attribution was done at the transport boundary per HTTP request instead of per logical model invocation, causing batched embedding requests with partial failures to misattribute consumed tokens; 2) Reranker paths that consume multiple embedding vectors and then call a small LLM to produce a selection were charging only the upstream embeddings or double-charging depending on retry paths; 3) Tool-call wrappers occasionally recorded only metadata from the parent request and then emitted downstream model calls that were billed under a generic internal key. Goal: Implement a deterministic, auditable attribution model that assigns every billed unit (token, embedding vector, model invocation) to a canonical owner id and reason code, supports partial-failure reconciliation, and integrates with rate-limit/quota windows so customers see consistent debits and automatic backfill/credits where appropriate.
acceptance_criteria: Every model invocation and token/embedding unit persisted in usage DB includes: canonical_customer_id, endpoint_type (embedding|rerank|tool|structured), model_id, sequence_length, invocation_id and attribution_reason_code.

Batched embedding requests that partially fail must generate reconciled usage rows: successful items billed to customer, failed items produce zero cost and a reconciliation entry linking to failure reason.
Reranker flows that call multiple models produce per-invocation charges (not aggregated) so operators and customers can trace exact sources of spend.
Tool-call derived downstream invocations are attributed to the originating API key with an additional tag tool_call_id and do not create orphaned generic-billing entries.
Rate limit quotas decrement deterministically based on canonical counts; quota windows remain consistent across retries and redirect/fallback paths.
Full unit tests and integration tests covering partial failures, retry semantics (idempotent and non-idempotent paths), and cross-service attribution.
Performance impact: end-to-end p95 latency increase for metering path < 3ms and no measurable change in token throughput for dedicated pools under test workloads.
rollout_plan: 1) Feature branch + unit tests; run local replay harness on duplicated production traces (embeddings/rerank/toolcall heavy traces).
2) Deploy flags: enable attribution tagging at ingest (off by default), run for 10% of keys in shadow mode for 48h to compare outputs and reconcile divergences.
3) Enable for 100% in shadow mode for 72h while running live reconciliation job that emits proposed credits for mismatches; validate credit totals against expected accounting.
4) Turn on live attribution for small customer cohort (10 customers) with CS/finance informed; monitor billing dashboards and respond to disputes.
5) Full rollout after two-week validation and org sign-off; automated backfill to correct past 7 days of high-severity mischarges and manual adjudication for older disputes.
Rollback: feature flag off plus negative-credit reversal for any misapplied charges; issue postmortem if > 0.5% of daily billing volume affected.
testing_plan: Unit tests for attribution mapper covering: batching, partial failures, retry idempotency, and tool-call propagation.
Integration tests using the replay harness (replay-service) with 1M-record trace sampling of last 7 days embedding/rerank traffic.
End-to-end charge validation: synthetic workload that mixes batch sizes (1-512), simulated partial node failures, and tool-call fanouts; compare invoices before/after change.
Load test on staging with dedicated pool to confirm metric overhead and latency budget for metering path.
Audit process: run a reconciliation worker that produces a diff report (current-billing vs new-attribution) and surface top 20 customers with the largest deltas to Billing/Finance for sign-off.
